inserts.macbeth-605: DUNCAN. O my most worthy cousin! Just now the sin of my ingratitude was weighing on me. You are so far ahead of me that even the swiftest reward is too slow to catch up with you. I wish you had deserved less, so that my thanks and payment could have matched what you are owed! All I can say is that you are owed more than everything I have could ever pay.
inserts.macbeth-710: LADY MACBETH. What news do you bring?
inserts.macbeth-732: LADY MACBETH. The raven croaking out Duncan's fatal arrival under my battlements is hoarse with it. Come, you spirits that serve murderous thoughts, strip me of my woman's nature here, and fill me from head to toe, brimful, with the most terrible cruelty! Thicken my blood; block every path that pity could take to reach me, so that no natural stirrings of conscience can shake my savage purpose or come between it and its fulfillment! Come to my woman's breasts and turn my milk to bitter gall, you agents of murder, wherever you invisibly wait to help nature do harm! Come, thick night, and wrap yourself in the darkest smoke of hell, so that my sharp knife cannot see the wound it makes, and heaven cannot peer through the blanket of the dark to cry, "Stop, stop!"
inserts.macbeth-752: LADY MACBETH. Great Glamis! Worthy Cawdor! Greater than both, by the "all hail" still to come! Your letters have carried me beyond this ignorant present, and I already feel the future in this very moment.
inserts.macbeth-1009: BANQUO. Give me my sword. Who's there?
inserts.macbeth-1065: MACBETH. Is this a dagger I see in front of me, with its handle turned toward my hand? Come, let me grab you. I don't have you, and yet I still see you. Deadly vision, can I not feel you as well as see you? Or are you only a dagger of the mind, a false creation coming from my fevered brain? I can still see you, as solid-looking as this one I'm drawing now. You're leading me the way I was already going, and I was going to use a weapon just like you. Either my eyes are being fooled by my other senses, or they are worth all the rest put together. I still see you, and on your blade and handle there are drops of blood that weren't there before. There's no such thing. It's this bloody business that is making my eyes see it. Now, over half the world, nature seems dead, and wicked dreams deceive the sleepers behind their curtains. Witches perform their rites to pale Hecate, and withered Murder, roused by his sentry the wolf, whose howl is his watch-call, moves toward his target like a ghost, with stealthy steps, with the strides of Tarquin going to his rape. You firm, solid earth, don't hear my steps or which way they go, in case your very stones chatter about where I am and break the horrible silence that suits this moment. While I stand here making threats, he lives. Words only cool the heat of action.
inserts.macbeth-1097: MACBETH. I go, and it is done. The bell invites me. Don't hear it, Duncan, because it is a death bell that summons you to heaven or to hell.
inserts.macbeth-1315: MACDUFF. Our knocking has woken him. Here he comes.
inserts.macbeth-1401: MACDUFF. Wake up, wake up! Ring the alarm bell! Murder and treason! Banquo and Donalbain! Malcolm! Wake up! Shake off this soft sleep, which only imitates death, and look at death itself! Up, up, and see an image of Judgment Day! Malcolm! Banquo! Rise up as if from your graves and walk like ghosts to face this horror!
inserts.macbeth-1427: MACDUFF. O Banquo, Banquo! Our royal master has been murdered!
inserts.macbeth-1516: BANQUO. Once we have covered our half-dressed bodies, which are suffering in the cold, let us meet and examine this most bloody deed, to learn more about it. Fears and doubts are shaking us. I put myself in the great hand of God, and from there I will fight against the hidden purpose behind this treacherous crime.
inserts.macbeth-1602: ROSS. How are things in the world now, sir?
inserts.macbeth-1745: MACBETH. Let everyone spend his time as he likes until seven tonight. To make company all the more welcome, I will keep to myself until supper. Until then, God be with you.
inserts.macbeth-1752: MACBETH. You there, a word with you. Are those men waiting for my orders?
inserts.macbeth-1763: MACBETH. To be king is nothing unless I am safely king. My fears of Banquo go deep, and his royal nature has something in it that ought to be feared. He dares a great deal, and on top of that fearless temper he has the wisdom to guide his courage so that it acts safely. There is no one but him whose existence I fear, and next to him my guiding spirit is cowed, just as Mark Antony's was said to be by Caesar's. He scolded the witches when they first called me king, and ordered them to speak to him. Then, like prophets, they hailed him as the father of a line of kings. On my head they placed a crown that will bear no fruit, and put a barren scepter in my grip, to be wrenched away by a hand not of my family, with no son of mine succeeding me. If that is so, I have defiled my mind for Banquo's children. For them I have murdered the gracious Duncan, poisoned my own peace only for them, and handed my eternal soul to the devil, the enemy of mankind, to make them kings, to make Banquo's seed kings! Rather than that, come, fate, into the arena, and fight me to the death! Who's there?
inserts.macbeth-1791: MACBETH. Now go to the door and wait there until we call.
inserts.macbeth-1795: MACBETH. Wasn't it yesterday that we spoke together?
inserts.macbeth-1907: MACBETH. It is settled. Banquo, if your soul's flight is going to find heaven, it must find it tonight.
inserts.macbeth-1939: LADY MACBETH. What's this, my lord? Why do you keep to yourself, with only the most miserable fantasies for company, dwelling on thoughts that should have died with the people you are thinking about? What can't be remedied shouldn't be worried over. What's done is done.
inserts.macbeth-2290: MACBETH. We drink to everyone, and to him, and to all good wishes for all.
inserts.macbeth-2320: MACBETH. There. Now that it's gone, I'm a man again. Please, stay seated.
inserts.macbeth-2437: HECATE. Listen! I'm being called. See, my little spirit sits in a foggy cloud and waits for me.
inserts.macbeth-2698: MACBETH. What is this, rising like the child of a king, wearing the crown, the symbol of sovereignty, on his baby brow?
inserts.macbeth-3014: FIRST MURDERER. You young spawn of a traitor!
inserts.macbeth-3476: GENTLEWOMAN. Look, here she comes! This is exactly how she does it, and, upon my life, she is fast asleep. Watch her. Stay hidden.
inserts.macbeth-3666: MACBETH. May the devil turn you black, you pale-faced fool! Where did you get that stupid goose look?
inserts.macbeth-3692: MACBETH. Seyton! I am sick at heart when I see— Seyton, I say! This attack will either secure me forever or throw me from my throne now. I have lived long enough. My life has withered into its autumn, the yellow leaf, and the things that should come with old age, like honor, love, obedience and crowds of friends, I must not expect to have. Instead I have curses, not loud but deep, and respect paid only with the lips, empty words that my people's hearts would gladly refuse me but don't dare to. Seyton!
inserts.macbeth-3862: MACBETH. What was that cry about?
inserts.macbeth-3883: MACBETH. You've come to use your tongue. Tell your story quickly.
